evidence.mission_note: A local manual, naturally aspirated BRZ fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and resells easily. The visible aftermarket aero makes use and modification history the deciding question.
evidence.rationale: The photos establish a red manual first-generation BRZ sitting on a Toyota dealer lot in Salinas, with straight glossy paint and no visible collision damage. They also show an aftermarket carbon-fibre trunk lid with wing, apparent aftermarket diffuser/splitters and an aftermarket shift knob. Two attached photos (a green widebody FR-S and a Porsche Boxster) are not this car and were disregarded. The listing asks $19,999 while the windshield sticker reads $18,999; both are at or above the $15,871-$19,037 fair-value range. Clean title, one owner, 51,610 miles and 'well maintained' are claims only: no VIN, no invoices, and the Carfax link was not examined. Track use, tune/header status, tire age, clutch health and the underside all remain unknown. The 2013 valve-spring and 2018-2019 fuel-pump recalls do not apply to a 2016 by the profile's scope.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, the out-the-door price (resolving $19,999 vs $18,999), a full mod/track-use disclosure, and permission for a PPI at a nearby independent shop, then pull the Carfax and NHTSA recall check on that VIN.
